source_language_policy.notes: All 104 current learn-from languages may explain the lesson from the learner's existing language. These records are source/comparison support, not a promise that the language is teachable as a grammar target.

required_assets: at least one structured grammar form
target_language_policy.notes: This lesson deliberately implements all current Tier 1 and Tier 2 languages as learning targets. Tier 3 remains reading/games plus source-language comparison only.

full.description: Structured grammatical-number rules exist and the language may be selected as a learning target for this lesson.

comparison_only.description: The language has a native grammatical-number comparison record and may be used as a source/explanation language, but this lesson does not teach it as a target.

unavailable.description: No current learn-from language is unavailable as a source comparison language in this family.

learning_from_language.rendering_behavior: Show the native-language explanation of how that language handles grammatical number, then contrast it with the selected target language.

learning_language_full.rendering_behavior: Show the target system, then teach its number formation, obligatoriness, agreement, and meaningful exceptions from structured rule data.

promotion_rules: Only Tier 1 and Tier 2 may be grammar-learning targets under the current product registry policy.
Tier 3 remains comparison_only even when a native comparison blurb exists.
Do not infer singular/plural as the only possible number inventory.
Do not promote a target unless its grammar record is lesson_ready and contains structured rules.
Generated native blurbs remain machine-level candidates until the normal language-review ladder promotes them.
